verses.text: “You shall not spread a false report. Don’t join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
“You shall not follow a crowd to do evil. You shall not testify in court to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
You shall not favor a poor man in his cause.
“If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again.
If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him, you shall surely help him with it.
“You shall not deny justice to your poor people in their lawsuits.
“Keep far from a false charge, and don’t kill the innocent and righteous: for I will not justify the wicked.
“You shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who have sight and perverts the words of the righteous.
“You shall not oppress an alien, for you know the heart of an alien, since you were aliens in the land of Egypt.
“For six years you shall sow your land, and shall gather in its increase,

but the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the poor of your people may eat; and what they leave the animal of the field shall eat. In the same way, you shall deal with your vineyard and with your olive grove.
“Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.
“Be careful to do all things that I have said to you; and don’t invoke the name of other gods or even let them be heard out of your mouth.
“You shall observe a feast to me three times a year.

You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the time appointed in the month Abib (for in it you came out of Egypt), and no one shall appear before me empty.
And the feast of harvest, the first fruits of your labors, which you sow in the field; and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in your labors out of the field.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord Yahweh.
“You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. The fat of my feast shall not remain all night until the morning.
The first of the first fruits of your ground you shall bring into the house of Yahweh your God. “You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
“Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. Don’t provoke him, for he will not pardon your disobedience, for my name is in him.
But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.
For my angel shall go before you, and bring you in to the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I will cut them off.
You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor follow their practices, but you shall utterly overthrow them and demolish their pillars.
You shall serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you.
No one will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.
I will send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
I will send the hornet before you, which will drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before you.
I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

I will set your border from the Red Sea even to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me, for if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.”

footnotes.content: A false word causes so much sorrow. The Lord knows how quickly lies spread through a community like poison. When you speak, speak truth—and refuse the hand of anyone asking you to witness to what you know is false.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The crowd's voice is loud, but it is not always the Lord's voice. How easy to lose yourself in the press of many, agreeing to bend justice just to fit in. Stand alone if you must—truth is worth more than belonging.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pity can cloud judgment. The poor deserve justice, yes—but not favor that distorts it. Fair judgment means the same standard for rich and poor alike. This is how we honor both the hungry and the truthful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Enemy's ox or donkey—a creature without choice in the quarrel. The Lord asks kindness even toward the property of those who oppose you. This is radical mercy, learned early: return what is lost, period.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The one who hates you struggles under the weight—and the Lord says, help. This is the hard road: compassion is not weakness but obedience. When you lift that burden, you are lifting someone the Lord loves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The poor have fewer voices to speak for them in court. The Lord takes their cause personally. If you sit in judgment, remember the weight of your word on those without power—they need your honesty most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Innocent blood cries out from the ground. The Lord will not justify falsehood that murders. When we speak in court or in whispers, we are either protecting life or ending it—there is no neutral ground here.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A bribe is a small death. Gold in the hand clouds the mind and twists words that should point straight to truth. The righteous person learns early to refuse it, even when no one watches.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You have been the stranger, the outsider. Egypt was not your home and they knew it. Now the Lord tells Israel: remember that loneliness. When you see the foreigner, you know their fear—show them the mercy you once needed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six years of labor, then the land rests. The Lord builds rhythms into creation itself—work and rest, taking and giving back. To honor these seasons is to trust that He will provide in the gap.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fallow year feeds the poor and the beasts alike. Generosity grows from the soil itself when you let it lie. The Lord shows here that abundance for others is not loss—it is obedience that multiplies blessing back to you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rest is not laziness—it is worship. Even the ox and donkey are given breath. The Lord insists on it because He knows we forget how. The servant, the alien, your own hands deserve the Sabbath's quiet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do not even let other gods be heard from your mouth. Words are seeds—careless speech about false gods plants confusion in listening hearts. Keep your tongue clean for the Lord's name alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three times a year, stop and gather. The Lord marks seasons of remembrance. These feasts stitch community back together and remind each generation of what He has done. Gathering together is how we remember together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Unleavened bread in Abib—the very month of exodus. Eating without yeast is eating the memory of haste, of departure, of deliverance. No one comes empty because the feast itself is the gift, and your presence honors it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Harvest and ingathering—the Lord marks both the bloom and the reaping. Gratitude moves through the whole year. Each feast names a different mercy: departure, firstfruits, home-bringing. This is how a people stays tender toward their God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All males appear before the Lord Yahweh. This is pilgrimage—a journey toward the holy, a visible showing-up. In gathering, we confess that we belong to Him and that He draws us near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blood and leaven do not mix at the feast; the fat does not linger overnight. These details teach cleanness and urgency. Your offering is not casual—it requires care, freshness, and the acknowledgment that you cannot hold the holy past its time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Firstfruits go to the Lord's house, and a young goat does not boil in its mother's milk—a mercy even in death. The law reminds Israel: the Lord owns the first and the best, and tenderness toward life matters even in small things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An angel sent ahead to guard the way and bring them to the place prepared. The Lord does not ask them to wander alone—He posts a guardian. This is the pattern of grace: Someone goes before, Someone watches, Someone has already readied the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Listen to the angel's voice and do not provoke him, for the Lord's name is in him. To disobey the messenger is to disobey the One who sends. Obedience to what God sends—even a guide we cannot see—is the way to life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you listen and obey all that I speak, I will be enemy to your enemies, helper to your helpers. The Lord stakes His own honor on Israel's faithfulness. Obedience invites Him to fight on your behalf.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The angel will bring them into Canaan and cut off the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, Canaanite, Hivite, and Jebusite. The Lord names the enemies plainly and promises their removal. Conquest is not accident—it is His stated intention, guided and accomplished.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do not bow to their gods or serve them—overthrow them, demolish their pillars. The Lord demands exclusive allegiance. The old religions of Canaan must be dismantled, not merely abandoned. This is commitment with force.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Serve the Lord your God, and He will bless bread, water, and health. The covenant is plain: faithfulness brings provision and healing. The Lord is not distant—He touches the daily necessities of life itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No miscarriage or barrenness in your land; He will fulfill your days. The Lord promises fruitfulness and length of life. This is blessing at the most intimate level—the womb, the generations, the years granted. Obedience is fertile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terror and confusion will come upon the enemies—they will turn and flee. The Lord fights by unsettling the hearts of those opposed to His people. This is psychological victory, a sign that the Lord goes before them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hornets will drive out the Hivite, Canaanite, and Hittite. Even small creatures become instruments of the Lord's purpose. He does not rely on Israel's strength alone—He uses what already inhabits the land to clear the way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will not drive them out in one year, lest the land become desolate and wild beasts multiply. Even conquest follows wisdom—rushing to victory can create chaos worse than the battle. The Lord paces His purpose carefully.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Little by little the Lord drives them out as Israel increases and inherits. Growth and displacement move together—as the covenant people grow strong, the land becomes theirs. This is the rhythm of God's kingdom: growth that displaces the old.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Border from Red Sea to Philistine sea, wilderness to the River—the Lord defines the land explicitly. Promise is specific, mapped, handed into Israel's hand. The inheritance is not vague but real geography, real possession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Make no covenant with them or their gods. Compromise here is death—a treaty with idolaters will pull the people away from the Lord. Separation is not cruelty but the price of faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let them not dwell in your land, or they will make you sin and their gods become a snare. The Lord knows the human heart's weakness—proximity to idolatry is its own temptation. Some separations protect us from ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
